items.q: Match each crystal with its shape — 1) Uric acid 2) Calcium oxalate dihydrate 3) Struvite (MgNH4PO4) … A) Coffin lid appearance B) Rhomboid crystals C) Bipyramidal / envelope shaped
items.exp: Uric acid – rhomboid; calcium oxalate dihydrate – bipyramidal/envelope; struvite – coffin lid. (Book p747)

items.q: Match each crystal with its description — 1) Calcium oxalate monohydrate 2) Calcium phosphate 3) Cystine … A) Hexagonal crystal B) Dumb bell shaped C) Star shaped in alkaline urine
items.exp: Calcium oxalate monohydrate – dumb bell; calcium phosphate – star shaped (alkaline urine); cystine – hexagonal. (Book p747)

items.q: The coffin-lid crystal with the formula MgNH4PO4 is:
Star-shaped crystals forming in alkaline urine are:
items.exp: Calcium phosphate (in alkaline urine): star shaped. (Book p747)

items.q: All of the following crystal-shape pairs are as printed EXCEPT:
opts: Calcium oxalate monohydrate - dumb bell shaped
items.exp: Uric acid crystals are rhomboid; envelope shape belongs to calcium oxalate dihydrate. (Book p747)

items.q: The broom brush appearance on urine microscopy belongs to crystals of:
items.exp: Amoxicillin crystal: broom brush appearance. (Book p747)

items.q: Fill up: The hexagonal crystals seen on urine microscopy are ______ crystals.
Which crystal statement is TRUE as per the figure labels?
opts: Calcium oxalate monohydrate is dumb bell shaped while the dihydrate is envelope shaped
Calcium oxalate monohydrate is envelope shaped while the dihydrate is dumb bell shaped
items.exp: Monohydrate – dumb bell; dihydrate – bipyramidal/envelope; cholesterol crystals are listed without those shapes. (Book p747)

items.q: A stone former's microscopy shows bipyramidal, envelope-shaped crystals. The crystal type is:
items.exp: Calcium oxalate dihydrate: bipyramidal/envelope shaped. (Book p747)
